polity.question: Who was the first President of India?
polity.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India (1950-1962)

polity.question: Which article deals with the Right to Equality?
polity.explanation: Article 14 deals with Equality before law

polity.question: The 42nd Amendment is also known as:
polity.explanation: 42nd Amendment (1976) is known as 'Mini Constitution' due to extensive changes

polity.question: Who was the first Chief Justice of India?
polity.explanation: H. J. Kania was the first Chief Justice of India (1950-1951)

polity.question: Which schedule deals with Anti-Defection law?
polity.explanation: 10th Schedule deals with Anti-Defection law (52nd Amendment 1985)

polity.question: The concept of 'Basic Structure' was established in which case?
polity.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) established basic structure doctrine

polity.question: Who appoints the Prime Minister of India?
polity.explanation: President appoints the Prime Minister under Article 75

polity.question: Which article gives the President ordinance-making power?
polity.explanation: Article 123 gives the President ordinance-making power

polity.question: The maximum strength of Lok Sabha is:
polity.explanation: Maximum strength of Lok Sabha is 552 (543 elected + 2 nominated + 50 from states)

polity.question: Which writ means 'command to perform public duty'?
polity.explanation: Mandamus means 'we command' - orders a public authority to perform its duty

history.question: Who was the founder of the Indian National Congress?
history.explanation: A.O. Hume founded the Indian National Congress in 1885

history.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
history.explanation: Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919

history.question: Who gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan'?
history.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' during 1965 war

history.question: The Dandi March covered a distance of:
history.explanation: Dandi March covered 240 miles (390 km) from Sabarmati to Dandi

history.question: Who was the Viceroy during the Partition of Bengal?
history.explanation: Lord Curzon was the Viceroy during the Partition of Bengal (1905)

history.question: The Green Revolution was started in which decade?
history.explanation: Green Revolution started in the 1960s under M.S. Swaminathan

history.question: Which city was the capital of the Indus Valley Civilization?
history.explanation: Mohenjo-Daro was one of the major cities of the Indus Valley Civilization

history.question: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
history.explanation: Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942

history.question: Who was the last Viceroy of India?
history.explanation: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India (1947)

history.question: The Charter Act of 1813 ended whose trade monopoly?
history.explanation: Charter Act 1813 ended East India Company's trade monopoly (except tea and China)

geography.question: Which is the largest state of India by area?
geography.explanation: Rajasthan is the largest state by area (342,239 sq km)

geography.question: Which river is known as 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
geography.explanation: Kosi is known as 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to frequent floods

geography.question: Which is a Kharif crop?
geography.explanation: Rice is a Kharif crop (monsoon season)

geography.question: Which state is known as 'God's Own Country'?
geography.explanation: Kerala is known as 'God's Own Country'

geography.question: Which is the only floating lake in the world?
geography.explanation: Loktak Lake (Manipur) is the only floating lake in the world

geography.question: Hornbill Festival is celebrated in:
geography.explanation: Hornbill Festival is celebrated in Nagaland

geography.question: Which is the largest freshwater lake in Asia?
geography.explanation: Wular Lake (J&K) is the largest freshwater lake in Asia

geography.question: Which national park is famous for one-horned rhinoceros?
geography.explanation: Kaziranga National Park (Assam) is famous for one-horned rhinoceros

geography.question: Which state is called 'Land of Five Rivers'?
geography.explanation: Punjab is called 'Land of Five Rivers'

geography.question: Which place receives the highest rainfall in the world?
geography.explanation: Mawsynram (Meghalaya) receives the highest rainfall in the world

economy.question: Which plan focused on heavy industries?
economy.explanation: Second Plan (1956-61) focused on heavy industries

economy.question: Planning Commission was replaced by:
economy.explanation: NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission in 2015

economy.question: Which plan had 'Garibi Hatao' as slogan?
economy.explanation: Fourth Plan (1969-74) had 'Garibi Hatao' as slogan

current-affairs.explanation: UNESCO headquarters is in Paris, France

current-affairs.explanation: International Court of Justice (ICJ) is in The Hague

current-affairs.explanation: SAARC headquarters is in Kathmandu, Nepal

current-affairs.question: Which organization publishes the Human Development Index?
current-affairs.explanation: UNDP publishes the Human Development Index (HDI)

current-affairs.question: Corruption Perceptions Index is published by:
current-affairs.explanation: Transparency International publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index

current-affairs.question: Global Innovation Index is published by:
current-affairs.explanation: WIPO publishes the Global Innovation Index

current-affairs.question: Which organization is headquartered in Geneva?
current-affairs.explanation: WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland

current-affairs.question: World Bank headquarters is in:
current-affairs.explanation: World Bank headquarters is in Washington DC, USA
